items.name: TextRange
items.summary: A range in text, represented as a pair of [`TextSize`][struct@TextSize].

methods.name: add_end
methods.summary: Adds an offset to the end position.

methods.name: add_start
methods.summary: Adds an offset to the start position.

methods.name: at
methods.signature: fn at(offset: TextSize, len: TextSize) -> TextRange
methods.summary: Create a new `TextRange` with the given `offset` and `len` (`offset..offset + len`).

methods.name: checked_add
methods.summary: Add an offset to this range.

methods.name: checked_sub
methods.summary: Subtract an offset from this range.

methods.name: contains
methods.summary: Check if this range contains an offset.

methods.name: contains_inclusive
methods.summary: Check if this range contains an offset.

methods.name: contains_range
methods.summary: Check if this range completely contains another range.

methods.name: cover
methods.summary: Extends the range to cover `other` as well.

methods.name: cover_offset
methods.summary: Extends the range to cover `other` offsets as well.

methods.name: empty
methods.summary: Create a zero-length range at the specified offset (`offset..offset`).

methods.name: end
methods.summary: The end point of this range.

methods.name: intersect
methods.summary: The range covered by both ranges, if it exists. If the ranges touch but do not overlap, the output range is empty.

methods.name: is_empty
methods.summary: Check if this range is empty.

methods.name: len
methods.summary: The size of this range.

methods.name: new
methods.signature: const fn new(start: TextSize, end: TextSize) -> TextRange
methods.summary: Creates a new `TextRange` with the given `start` and `end` (`start..end`).

methods.name: ordering
methods.summary: Relative order of the two ranges (overlapping ranges are considered equal).

methods.name: start
methods.summary: The start point of this range.

methods.name: sub_end
methods.summary: Subtracts an offset from the end position.

methods.name: sub_start
methods.summary: Subtracts an offset from the start position.

methods.name: to_std_range
methods.summary: A convenience routine for converting this range to a standard library range that satisfies the `RangeBounds` trait.

methods.name: up_to
methods.summary: Create a range up to the given end (`..end`).

methods.name: with_end
methods.summary: Returns a new range with the end offset set to the value given and the start offset unchanged from this range.

methods.name: with_start
methods.summary: Returns a new range with the start offset set to the value given and the end offset unchanged from this range.
